_comment: Supervisor config for the Domain 4 loop, in METRES in TacFrame (ENU about
the surveyed anchor). Note this differs from the Brain's defaults, which
are in normalised estimator units (a 1x1 box, 8 cm spacing) because the
Brain flew a Crazyflie-scale dataset. Same struct, same gate, different
READ BY BOTH SIDES. The Rust binary parses this file, and
sim/orchestrator.py's Python pre-check loads the SAME file rather than
carrying its own copy. Two configs that drift apart produce an
inexplicable REJECT on a plan the planner was certain about.
max_cov_trace is the number Domain 1 is about. The live range-only
estimator holds sigma around 1.7 cm/axis in flight => trace ~0.0006, so
0.02 leaves an order of magnitude of headroom before the trust gate fires.
A conventionally-pinned estimator reports a comparable trace while being
1.16 m from truth, which is exactly why this gate cannot be the only thing
standing between a drifting estimate and a commanded vehicle.
_clock_note: max_estimate_age_ms is 1000, the value a real deployment should use.
It was 3000 under the previous host. The Rust gate measures freshness as
SystemTime::now() minus a unix-ms stamp, i.e. against the WALL clock, and
that host's wall clock was stepped ~1.3 s at a time by Hyper-V TimeSync --
so a 1000 ms window rejected plans that were perfectly fresh. The M1 does
not have that pathology and the window is back where it belongs.
The Python side was always immune: it times durations with
have to be wall clock for the cross-process contract, which is why both
clocks exist and why they must not be mixed. If you move this stack to a
host with a stepping clock, widen this number and treat every staleness
result measured there as having a noise floor the size of the step.
